# sigma_api_connector (Resource)

An API connector: defines how Sigma calls an external HTTP endpoint from within a workbook. `params_json`/`config_json` are forwarded verbatim (opaque JSON) and are **not** refreshed from GET, so there is no drift detection on those fields (same trade-off as `sigma_connection.details_json`).

## Example Usage

```terraform
# An API connector defines how Sigma calls an external HTTP endpoint from within
# a workbook. The url host must match the credential's allowlist.
resource "sigma_api_connector" "example" {
  name        = "example-data-api"
  description = "Fetches reference data from the example service"
  auth_id     = sigma_api_connector_credential.example.id

  params_json = jsonencode({
    method      = "GET"
    url         = "https://api.example.com/v1/data"
    headers     = []
    pathParams  = []
    queryParams = []
    body        = ""
  })
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Display name of the connector.
- `params_json` (String, Sensitive) JSON-encoded `params` object per Sigma's POST /v2/api-connectors schema: `method`, `url`, `headers`, `pathParams`, `queryParams`, `body`. The `url` host must match the credential's allowlist. Sensitive, since headers and query params can carry keys.

### Optional

- `auth_id` (String) ID of the `sigma_api_connector_credential` used for outbound auth. Omit for unauthenticated connectors.
- `config_json` (String) JSON-encoded optional `config` object per Sigma's POST /v2/api-connectors schema.
- `description` (String) Free-text description.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String)
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `updated_at` (String)

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import sigma_api_connector.example '<api_connector_id>'
```
